correctness.rationale: For a Gaussian matrix centered to the sum-zero tangent hyperplane, loss of a support function is unchanged by centering; the spherical width defect is (D+(G)+D+(-G))/||projected G||. One-sided zero loss exactly means top-k entries form a k-matching; uniform ranks yield (N)_k²/(N²)_k. For k~c sqrt N, top-ranked pair row/column collisions converge to marked Poisson intensity 2c² du dv on 0<u<v<1, giving mean c² per tail. Triple overlaps have vanishing expectation. Gaussian ranked extreme gaps scale as -log v/t_N; density 2v for v yields Exp(rate 2). Deleting weaker cells and inserting next ranked nonconflicting cells give a sandwich for actual k-matching optimization. Top/bottom rank sets couple asymptotically independently, and projected norm/sqrt(N²-1)->1, so total scaled defect tends to compound Poisson intensity 2c², Exp(2) jumps; no-loss atom e^-2c² is proved by collision counts rather than weak convergence. Independent exact enumeration confirmed the one-sided count at N=3,4,5, k<=N.
residual_risks: Poisson and Gaussian quantile steps are analytical, not verified by the finite checker.
No convergence-of-moments assertion or supercritical positive-loss scale.
